text: Large language models, or LLMs, are AI systems trained on enormous amounts of text from books, articles, and websites. They learn patterns in language by predicting the next word in a sentence, which lets them generate coherent responses. When you use an LLM, you give it a prompt—a question or instruction—and the model uses its training to produce a relevant answer. This is called prompt engineering, and the way you phrase your request greatly affects the quality of the output. LLMs can write essays, summarize information, and even code, but they are not truly intelligent. They can make mistakes, invent facts, or show bias from their training data. So, while they are powerful tools, you should always check their work.
